abstract: This postdoctoral research project develops and validates an uncertainty-aware, end-to-end decision framework for crop water-stress monitoring and irrigation decision support in row crops. It fuses multi-source Earth observation (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and, where available, high-resolution PlanetScope imagery), in-situ soil sensors, weather data and field observations into probabilistic estimates of the latent field state - root-zone soil moisture, crop water stress and canopy condition - carrying uncertainty honestly from observation to decision. Two interchangeable diagnostic routes share a single decision engine: a rigorous one-step probabilistic-fusion route (Route A), which feeds the satellite as one more covariate into a probabilistic machine-learning model (e.g. a Bayesian hierarchical model or Gaussian process) and goes straight to the field state with its uncertainty; and a lighter homogeneous-patch proxy route (Route B) that sidesteps the sub-pixel resolution problem by reading a nearby covarying patch the coarse pixel can resolve cleanly. From the diagnosed state onward the path is the same for both routes: the state drives uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration and counterfactual irrigation simulation over weather ensembles, recommending the option with the best expected economic return. The scientific novelty, argued against a systematic literature review, is the end-to-end coupling of learned multimodal fusion, explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation and economically optimised irrigation, which the literature reports as underdeveloped for row crops.
